issues.description: The template StockIngredient class exposes the ingredient quantity via a method named retrieveQuantity(), but other artifacts (the template Stock.java and Main.java caller code) and the solution use the conventional getter name getQuantity(). The problem statement also instructs students to "add getters for all the private fields." Because of this naming mismatch, calls to getQuantity() in Stock.java and Main.java do not compile against the template StockIngredient implementation, blocking students from building and running the project.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the getter name consistent with the rest of the code and with the problem statement. In src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java (template) either rename retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity() with the same behavior, or add a public getQuantity() method that returns the same value (e.g., public int getQuantity() { return retrieveQuantity(); }). Ensure callers and tests use getQuantity() consistently.
